newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes lower in ranged trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes lower in ranged trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed softer against the dollar on Monday after moving in a narrow range, with speculators sidelined and the exchange rate near the Central Bank's top level, dealers said.
The rupee closed at the Central Bank's selling price of 59.28, after opening at 59.27.

"Trading was very thin with imports being covered with dollars from the Central Bank, which has said it will not sell it (dollars) for anything but trade-backed transactions," said an American Express Bank dealer.

The dollar-rupee exchange rate has been around the Central Bank's top level since Thursday. This had an impact on call rates, which were pushed up on slight tightness in the money market, dealers said.

"Call money closed at eight percent after opening at 8.5 and even moving to 11 due to a tightness in the money, because banks have been buying dollars from the Central Bank for three days," said a Seylan Bank dealer.
